reproducibility.basis: All 18 Lean theorem names, axiom footprints (2 none, 1 [propext], 15 [propext, Quot.sound]), 16 certificate stems with exact rational witnesses and latencies (0.254-2.272 ms), and runner scripts are explicitly reported, though full Lean/Python source code resides in the linked repository outside the 4-page PDF.

rigor.basis: Constructive zero-sorry, zero-Classical.choice formalization paired with pure int/Fraction verification, strict parser hardening, and 60/60 adversarial rejections; scope exclusions (measure theory, 96-interval LP, external Taylor tail) are transparently stated, with minor notational shortcuts in Definition 1 Mode 3 and Table 1.

significance.basis: Substantially strengthens confidence in the algebraic bottlenecks of [1]—especially Lemma 4.4's degree-7 Bernstein positivity and Section 3's knapsack separations—while leaving [1]'s probabilistic arguments and 96-interval LP infeasibility proof of the 29/70 bound unformalized.

potential_errors: Definition 1 Mode 3 (p. 2) writes beta_k = sum_{j=0}^k (C(k,j)/C(7,j)) p_j of Lemma 4.4's polynomial P(b) over [l, r], without explicitly stating that p_j are the power-basis coefficients of the interval-reparameterized polynomial t |-> P(l + (r-l)t) on [0, 1] rather than raw coefficients of P(b).

Table 1 row 8 (threshold_tail_bound_monotone) writes '(gives (1-e)/(x-e) <= 1/x for D>0, x>e)', whereas for general D>0 the inequality yields (D-e)/(x-e) <= D/x and specializes to (1-e)/(x-e) <= 1/x only at normalization D=1.
Table 1 row 9 (clipped_optimum_variance_step_bound) summarizes the precondition as 'AllBounded c ds' without displaying the lower bound 0 <= d_i required for d_i^2 <= c * d_i to hold.

Table 1 row 16 (profile_stoploss_monotone_sandwich) proves only (y-x)S_y <= (y-x)S_x and D_y <= D_x from (y-x)S_y <= D_x - D_y, rather than Lemma 6.3(c)'s full upper bound D_x - D_y <= (y-x)S_x from the profile definition.

summary: This 4-page companion paper presents a constructive Lean 4.35.0 formalization (DelegationBounds.lean, 18 theorems with 0 sorry and 0 Classical.choice) and a pure-rational certificate auditor (DELEG-DC-CERT-1.0) covering the deterministic algebraic, 5-item knapsack impossibility, single-threshold/Efron-Stein, degree-7 Bernstein positivity, and seed-reserve/profile pillars of Abdi, Banihashem, Hajiaghayi, and Mittal [1] (arXiv:2611.33095). Every explicit rational identity, polynomial evaluation, Taylor partial sum, and Table 2 certificate witness in the PDF checks out exactly, and the authors transparently delimit what is excluded from Lean (measure-theoretic martingale/Harris-FKG steps, the 96-interval LP infeasibility proof of Theorem 5.1, Appendix A's DP, and the infinite Taylor tail > 0 in Theorem 12). Only minor notational/summary imprecisions appear in Definition 1 Mode 3 and Table 1, with no material objections invalidating the paper's claims.
weaknesses: The core probabilistic/measure-theoretic arguments and the 96-interval LP infeasibility computer proof of Theorem 5.1 (establishing the 29/70 lower bound in [1]) are not formalized in Lean 4; the Lean module verifies deterministic algebraic identities and finite-list/integer reductions.

As a 4-page summary referencing an external repository, full Lean 4 proof terms and Python verifier implementations cannot be audited directly from the PDF text alone (e.g., verifying that AllBounded enforces 0 <= d_i <= c or that Mode 3 reparameterizes P(b) to [l, r]).

Minor accounting detail: the text cites 60 live adversarial forgery attacks (16 global + 4x11 per-mode) plus 2 raw JSON IEEE-754/NaN checks alongside '63/63 pytest checks passing' without specifying the 63rd test case.
